artifact_contract: Design-level transition relation. It is not the serialization format for the Python enumerator's trace events; executable semantic invariants are checked in experiments/test_tr26_043_true_filtration.py.

semantics.coloring: Uniform balanced f:[n]->{-1,+1}; deferred decisions expose a uniformly random remaining sign at each genuinely new reveal.
semantics.tie_coins: Independent fair L/R bits, drawn only after equality of the two candidate absolute heights is known.
semantics.true_filtration_boundary: After a consume and before any newly exposed frontier is inspected. All prior inspections and used tie bits remain measurable, including an inspected but unconsumed frontier.

reveal_policy_parameter.eager: Inspect both active candidate colors before comparison, including at H=0.
reveal_policy_parameter.minimal: At H=0, where both candidate absolute heights are one independently of their colors, toss the tie coin first and inspect only the selected candidate. At nonzero H inspect both as required.

two_orders.probe: The steered path used to find balanced endpoints, block exhaustion, and descent endpoints.
two_orders.output: The chain order after existential greedy gap filling; it need not equal the probe order inside a gap.

two_block_transitions.guard: both blocks active, H=0, and reveal_policy=minimal
operation: Recognize the candidate absolute heights are both one without inspecting either color.
Reveal a fair L/R tie coin.
Reveal only the selected frontier and prepare to consume it.

two_block_transitions.guard: at least one local block is active and TB-1 does not apply
operation: For each active block, identify its current frontier from (segment,a,b).
Retain any frontier already in revealed_colors.
Reveal each unknown active frontier; branch by the exact remaining plus/minus counts.
Do not erase the unchosen frontier from revealed_colors.

two_block_transitions.guard: both blocks active and the two candidate absolute heights differ
operation: Choose the block whose frontier minimizes |H+f(frontier)|.

two_block_transitions.guard: both blocks active and the two candidate absolute heights are equal
operation: Reveal one fresh fair tie coin.
Choose L or R according to that coin and append it to tie_outcomes.
Choose the unique active block; no tie coin is sampled.
Append the chosen element to probe_order and assigned_set.
Increment a or b; update H and D=a-b.
Preserve every revealed value, especially the unchosen frontier.
If |H| crossed 1->2, start an above-band excursion; if it returned to <=1, close the excursion and update the last balanced visit.

multiscale_transitions.guard: the current segment has an even-size split and the effective unassigned size meets the v0 invariant
operation: Continue the local two-block process from the recorded start indices (a0,b0).
Record every visit to |H|<=1 and every intervening probe gap.

multiscale_transitions.guard: two consecutive recorded visits to |H|<=1 exist
operation: Let the gap be the set difference between the two probe endpoints.
Replace the probe order inside that gap by some 1-balanced order supplied existentially by Lemma 6.1.
The v0 paper does not select a unique order when more than one is valid.

multiscale_transitions.guard: the consume just exhausted one local block
operation: Set the residual to the unconsumed suffix of the other half.
Save the last |H|<=1 probe endpoint and the tail from that endpoint to exhaustion.

multiscale_transitions.guard: residual size is at least M0 and the residual has an even-size split
operation: Start a fresh local grid on the residual at (0,0).
Run the same true-filtration two-block transitions until the first visit to |H|<=1.
Retain any unconsumed revealed frontier in the next scale state.
Gap-fill the union of the prior-scale tail and the descent probe elements.
Create the next scale frame on the residual with start indices equal to the descent endpoint.
Gap-fill the prior-scale tail together with every residual element, ending at [n].

multiscale_transitions.guard: a filler order has been selected
operation: Append the chosen filler order to output_chain_order.
The probe observations remain in the true filtration even if output order differs.

partiality_of_v0.condition: a recursive residual has odd cardinality
partiality_of_v0.reason: Definition 3.1 is supplied only for an even segment split into equal halves; residual parity is unrestricted.

partiality_of_v0.condition: a gap has more than one valid 1-balanced ordering
partiality_of_v0.reason: Lemma 6.1 proves existence and its h=0 branch says any element; no canonical filler is fixed.

partiality_of_v0.condition: the initial effective size is below M0/2
partiality_of_v0.reason: Theorem 8.1 initializes invariant (iii) with m'_0=n but states m'_j>=M0/2; a finite-n completion is not specified.

The displayed block-deviation event gives an upper bound on m_{j+1}, not the lower bound cited for this logarithmic comparison. Even if the missing lower bound m_{j+1}>=(m'_j)^(2/3)/2 were assumed, the divisor two requires additive constant (3/2)ln 2, approximately 1.03972, rather than the printed +1.

reachable_set_conventions.two_block_probe: Exactly enumerated by experiments/tr26_043_true_filtration.py. Every set is a union of a left prefix and right prefix.
reachable_set_conventions.multiscale_probe: A union of completed contributions outside nested residuals plus a current local prefix pair; only defined while all required splits are defined.
reachable_set_conventions.multiscale_output: Not a unique set without either enumerating every Lemma 6.1-valid filler or adding a filler policy.
reachable_set_conventions.definition_7_4_set_system: An explicit over-approximation by all valid multiscale decompositions/local patterns; it is not the same object as the exact set of states reached by one unspecified builder execution.
